27 An aircraft flies at a velocity vs directly away from a stationary observer.
The aircraft emits a sound of constant frequency.
The speed of sound in air is v.
The frequency of the sound heard by the observer on the ground is 500 Hz.
The speed of the aircraft is increased so that it flies away from the observer at a greater velocity.
The observer now hears a sound of frequency 250 Hz.
Which expression gives the new velocity of the aircraft?
+
s
v
v
C
2vs + v
D
2vs – v
A
2(v + vs)
B
2

hints: Notice the source moves directly away from a stationary observer, so the observed wavelength is stretched by the source speed $v_s$.
Recall the receding-source Doppler equation $f_o = f_s v/(v+v_s)$ where $f_s$ is the constant emitted frequency.
Use that $f_o$ halves from $500 \text{ Hz}$ to $250 \text{ Hz}$ while $f_s$ and $v$ stay constant, so the denominator $v+v_{new}$ must be twice $v+v_s$.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: stationary observer and source receding at $v_s$, so observed frequency is $f_o = f_s \times v/(v+v_s)$ where $v$ is speed of sound and $f_s$ is the unknown constant source frequency.
Write the first case with $500 \text{ Hz}$: $500 = f_s v/(v+v_s)$.
Write the second case with unknown new speed $v_{new}$ and $250 \text{ Hz}$: $250 = f_s v/(v+v_{new})$.
Divide the two equations to eliminate $f_s v$: $500/250 = (v+v_{new})/(v+v_s)$.
Rearrange for the new velocity: $v_{new} = 2v_s+v$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is larger than $v$ by $2v_s+v$ and does not satisfy the ratio of observed frequencies for a receding source.

B.explanation: This is an average of $v$ and $v_s$ and would give a higher observed frequency, not the halved $250 \text{ Hz}$ frequency.

C.explanation: Halving of observed frequency from $500 \text{ Hz}$ to $250 \text{ Hz}$ requires $v+v_{new}=2(v+v_s)$, giving $v_{new}=2v_s+v$.

D.explanation: This subtracts $v$ instead of adding $v$ and would make the denominator $2(v_s+v)-2v$, which does not give half the frequency.
